newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Soyuz delivers relief crew to troubled Mir.
newsitem.headline: Russian Soyuz delivers relief crew to troubled Mir.

text.p: A Soyuz spacecraft with a two-man Russian relief crew docked successfully at 1702 GMT on Thursday with the crippled Mir space station, Mission Control said.
A wave of applause burst out at the tense Mission Control outside Moscow and a huge sign "Congratulations" appeared on the screen after the docking took place a minute ahead of schedule.

Commander Anatoly Solovyov, 49, and 43-year-old flight engineer Pavel Vinogradov are scheduled to meet the current three-man crew at about 1830 GMT when the hatch between Mir and Souyz will be opened. The new crew face a daunting task of trying to restore power to the ageing station.

Mir suffered its worst accident on June 25, when a supply ship pierced its Spektr scientific module during a manual docking manoeuvre. Cosmonauts had to unplug power cables leading from Spektr's solar panels as they fled the module and sealed it. The accident deprived Mir of up to half of its power supply.

The two Russians, including commander Vasily Tsibliyev who has developed a stress-imposed heart problem, are scheduled to return to Earth on August 14. British-American physicist Michael Foale will remain on board until late September.

Mission Control operators smiled and shook hands warmly as the head of the Russian Space Agency Yuri Koptev, officials from the U.S. agency NASA and representatives from the European Space Agency looked on in relief.
